o1.biggest_strength: The 8+ segment is sized correctly and the revenue math checks out per 1,000 switchers, at three churn levels including the 4.1% case I hoped to see. The customer messages are in our voice and include the invite email, a pricing page card and a public post. Each says plainly that nothing changes for current prices.
o1.biggest_mistake: The first test invites only Essentials 8+ customers, so the Team downgrade risk it names is never measured before launch. It is only caught by a rule after launch. The math is also per 1,000 switchers, with no company-level view the board can read against two quarters.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Include Team 8+ customers in the test so cannibalization is measured. Show net company revenue at month 6 with a downside case. Offer yearly billing at the switch as a cheap, honest push, not just as a later test. Drop the awkward 'bad news first' line.

o2.biggest_strength: The math is built up to a net company figure: +$2.7k on day one and +$23k a month by month 6, after Team downgrades. It adds a downside case and a break-even, which is that the plan loses money if more than about 1 in 3 Team 8+ customers move down. The test invites Team 8+ customers too, with clear go and stop thresholds on switch rate, churn and downgrades.
o2.biggest_mistake: The 5% churn for switchers and the 50% switch rate are assumed, not grounded, and the model is a bit dense. The customer copy is thinner than it should be: it has no pricing page text, and the email uses a placeholder for the current bill. Yearly billing appears only as a line inside the switch offer.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add pricing page copy and a launch post draft. Offer yearly billing to existing monthly customers on its own, as the fastest win. Show why the 5% churn assumption is reasonable, and simplify the revenue table for the team.

reason: Both pick the same flat Agency plan for the 8+ group and get the numbers right. I would act on Output 2 because it shows what the plan does to the company's total revenue, including the Team downgrade risk and a downside case, and it tests that risk before launch. Output 1 has nicer customer copy, but its test leaves the biggest risk unmeasured.
